title: Sidney Bechet asleep on the Smoky Mary
summary: Dawson tells how he fetched a sleeping young Bechet from the train to Milneburg picnics, with Perez and Palao in the band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Yeah. The other night also we were talking about Sidney Bechet.
Oh, yeah. He told that funny story about him being on the Smoky Mary. Tell us about it.

We used to play at Millenburg for picnics out there. Those were only picnics. And Sidney Bechet, he was playing clarinet with us, you see. And well, and Manuel Perez was playing trumpet. And we had the same fella Jimmy Pollard playing violin too. He used to play with his two over there. And we'd play them picnics. Cause we used to take a man when needed a man on the picnic. We'd have extra man when needed, you see. And Sidney Bechet would get on that old Smoky Mary, you know, that running out the Millenburg and that we'd be short of waiting for him. And we couldn't find, we didn't know the trouble. They'd send me out there to look to the train and see if I could locate him. Well, I'd go out there and I'd look on the train. I asked the conductor, I'd say, if you've seen a musician lately on this train, he said, the fella there back in the coach, they had been on there and made three trips. And he's got some kind of little box there that was his clarinet. Well, I'd go there and wake him up, you know, and bring him over to the saloon and wash his face and give him a glass of wine. And revive him up and come on back there and play the picnic. How'd he play in those days? Oh, he used to play, I'll tell you. Well, we had a regular Dixieland band too, you know. You know, we could play classic music too. That was Jim and Paul had nothing but the music. Emanuel Peres said he didn't carry nothing but the strictness music. Almost all the men in the band could read good. But they could play that Dixieland too.
